name: Human
description: Found in every terrain and environment, their curiosity and ambition drive them to explore every corner of the world, making them a ubiquitous and versatile race.

features.name: Tenacious
features.text: +1 to all skills and Initiative.

name: Dwarf
description: Dwarf, in the old language, means “stone.” You are resilient, solid, stout. Even when driven to exhaustion, you will not falter. Forgoing speed, you are gifted with physical vitality and a belly that can handle the finest (and worst) consumables this world has to offer.

features.name: Stout
features.text: +2 max Hit Dice, +1 max Wounds, –1 Speed. You know Dwarvish if your INT isn’t negative.
features.manualNote: Dwarvish is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Elf
description: Elves epitomize swiftness and grace. Their tall, slender forms belie their innate speed, grace, and wit. Formidable in both diplomacy and combat, elves strike swiftly, often preventing the worst by acting first.

features.name: Lithe
features.text: Advantage on Initiative, +1 Speed. You know Elvish if your INT isn’t negative.
features.manualNote: Elvish is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Halfling
description: Kind of like a human, but smaller (except for the feet). Where does our luck come from? Well… you know what they say about rabbit feet? Well, we’ve got feet for days compared to them. Imagine the amount of luck you could fit into these bad boys!

features.name: Elusive
features.text: +1 to Stealth. (1/Safe Rest) If you fail a save, you can succeed instead.

action.name: Elusive
action.text: (1/Safe Rest) If you fail a save, you can succeed instead.

features.manualNote: When you fail a save and use this, spend the use and treat the save as a success by hand.

name: Gnome
description: Eccentric, curious, and perpetually optimistic, gnomes are cheerful—especially when compared to their typically grumpier and larger kin, the dwarves. Known for their tinkering, spreading cheer, and playful antics, gnomes pursue their passions with a scatterbrained enthusiasm.

features.name: Optimistic
features.text: (Free Reaction, Reach 6) Allow an ally to reroll any 1 die; resets when healed to max HP. –1 Speed. You know Dwarvish if your INT isn’t negative (but you call it Gnomish, of course).

action.name: Optimistic
action.text: (Free Reaction, Reach 6) Allow an ally to reroll any 1 die; resets when healed to max HP.

features.manualNote: The ally rerolls the die themselves. Dwarvish (Gnomish) is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

source.note: Interpreted: “resets when healed to max HP” encoded as a 1-use resource recovered on healedToMax.
Interpreted: “resets when healed to max HP” encoded as a 1-use resource recovered on healedToMax.

name: Dragonborn
description: The soul of a dragon burns within you, the scales of your body are like forged steel. You are a kiln and your heritage the coals that stoke your flames. Call upon your wrath to speak in the tongue of your ancestors and imbue unbridled fury into your attacks.

features.name: Draconic Heritage
features.text: +1 Defense. (1/Safe Rest) Deal an additional LVL+KEY damage on an attack divided as you choose among any of the attack’s targets (recharges whenever you gain a Wound). You know Draconic if your INT isn’t negative.

action.name: Draconic Heritage
action.text: (1/Safe Rest) Deal an additional LVL+KEY damage on an attack divided as you choose among any of the attack’s targets (recharges whenever you gain a Wound).

features.manualNote: Add the LVL+KEY damage and divide it among targets by hand; restore the use by hand whenever you gain a Wound. Draconic is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Goblin
description: Green, cunning, and perpetually vilified, Goblins thrive on the edge of chaos. For a Goblin, vanishing into the shadows is not just a skill—it’s an identity. After all, what kind of Goblin would you be if you couldn’t slip away unnoticed?

features.name: Skedaddle
features.text: Can move 2 spaces for free after you become the target of an attack or negative effect (after damage, ignoring Difficult Terrain). You know Goblin if your INT isn’t negative.
features.manualNote: Move your token up to 2 spaces by hand after being targeted. Goblin is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Orc
description: Just when you think you’ve bested a mighty Orc, you’ve merely succeeded in rousing their anger. Engaging in combat with an Orc is no endeavor for the weak-willed. While others may cower before death’s approach, Orcs boldly defy its grasp.

features.name: Relentless
features.text: (1/Safe Rest) When you would drop to 0 HP, you may set your HP to LVL instead. +1 Might. You know Goblin if your INT isn’t negative (but you call it Orcish, of course).

action.name: Relentless
action.text: (1/Safe Rest) When you would drop to 0 HP, you may set your HP to LVL instead.

features.manualNote: When you would drop to 0 HP, spend the use and set your HP to your level by hand. Goblin (Orcish) is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Kobold
description: Small, often maniacal, and dragon-obsessed. Kobolds thrive in familial groups, working together and finding ingenious ways to survive despite their diminutive size. Underestimated by many, Kobolds prove time and again that even the smallest among us can wield great power.

features.name: Wily
features.text: Advantage on skill checks related to dragons and to Influence friendly creatures. (1/encounter) Force an enemy to reroll a non-critical attack against you. You know Draconic if your INT isn’t negative.

action.name: Wily
action.text: (1/encounter) Force an enemy to reroll a non-critical attack against you.

features.manualNote: Turn on the Wily advantage toggles when they apply; tell the GM to reroll the attack when you use the reroll. Draconic is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Fiendkin
description: Said to have been born from a cursed bloodline or from the union of man and fiend, Fiendkin often find themselves outcasts in society. Yet, they embody determination in the face of adversity. Their ancestors didn’t emerge from the depths of the Everflame to succumb to minor setbacks!

features.name: Flameborn
features.text: 1 neutral save is advantaged instead. You know Infernal if your INT isn’t negative.

choice.prompt: Choose 1 neutral save to make advantaged

features.manualNote: Infernal is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Bunbun
description: Bunbun are agile and unpredictable, using their powerful legs to leap great distances and catch foes off guard. Facing a Bunbun means contending with an opponent who can strike from unexpected angles and swiftly reposition themselves in the heat of battle.

features.name: Bunny Legs
features.text: (1/encounter) Before Interposing or after Defending (after damage), hop up to your Speed in any direction for free.

action.name: Bunny Legs
action.text: (1/encounter) Before Interposing or after Defending (after damage), hop up to your Speed in any direction for free.

features.manualNote: Move your token by hand when you use it.

name: Birdfolk
description: Birdfolk find sanctuary not in stone or chains, but within the boundless expanse of the sky. However, the gift of flight comes at a cost—hollow bones, and commensurate frailty.

features.name: Hollow Bones
features.text: You can fly as long as you are wearing armor no heavier than Leather. Crits against you are Vicious (the attacker rolls 1 additional die).
features.manualNote: Flying (only in Leather armor or lighter) and Vicious crits against you are handled by hand.

name: Celestial
description: Descendants of divine beings, Celestials carry an aura of nobility and grace. Their innate connection to the higher planes allows them to resist the effects of misfortune, standing strong where others may falter.

features.name: Highborn
features.text: Your disadvantaged save is neutral instead. You know Celestial if your INT isn’t negative.
features.manualNote: Celestial is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Changeling
description: Often hunted for their silver blood, Changelings are natural survivors, slipping into new identities with ease. Changelings that shift too often typically aren’t long for the world—they can struggle to remember who they once were, becoming little more than reflections of the faces they wear.

features.name: New Place, New Face
features.text: +2 Shifting Skill Points. You take on the appearance of any ancestry (transformation time 10 min). When you do, you may move your 2 Shifting Skill Points into any 1 skill.
features.manualNote: Track your 2 Shifting Skill Points by hand: put them in any 1 skill, and move them to any 1 skill when you transform (10 min).

name: Crystalborn
description: Formed from living crystal, the Crystalborn are beings of dazzling beauty and otherworldly toughness. Their translucent bodies refract light and sound, granting them unique abilities in combat.

features.name: Reflective Aura
features.text: (1/encounter) When you Defend, gain KEY Defense and deal KEY damage back to the attacker (ignoring their armor).

action.name: Reflective Aura
action.text: (1/encounter) When you Defend, gain KEY Defense and deal KEY damage back to the attacker (ignoring their armor).

features.manualNote: Add KEY to your Defense for that attack and deal KEY damage to the attacker by hand.

name: Dryad/Shroomling
description: Tied to the natural world, Dryads and Shroomlings embody the balance between flora and fauna. Their unique physiology releases toxic spores when harmed, providing a natural defense against those who dare to harm them.

features.name: Danger Pollen/Spores
features.text: Whenever you gain one or more Wounds, you excrete soporific spores: all adjacent enemies are Dazed. You know Elvish if your INT isn’t negative.
features.manualNote: When you gain Wounds, tell the GM all adjacent enemies are Dazed. Elvish is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Half-Giant
description: Towering beings whose strength is as immovable as the mountains they call home. Their sheer size and resilience make them fearsome opponents, capable of surviving even devastating blows.

features.name: Strength of Stone
features.text: (1/encounter) Force an enemy to reroll a crit against you. +2 Might. You know Dwarvish if your INT isn’t negative (but you call it Giant, of course).

action.name: Strength of Stone
action.text: (1/encounter) Force an enemy to reroll a crit against you.

features.manualNote: Tell the GM to reroll the crit when you use it. Dwarvish (Giant) is added automatically, but applies only if your INT isn’t negative; remove it by hand if your INT is negative.

name: Minotaur/Beastfolk
description: Minotaur and other Beastfolk embody a primal connection to The Wild, combining strength with natural agility. Their powerful build allows them to move swiftly, whether repositioning to outflank foes or charging in with unstoppable force.

features.name: Charge
features.text: When you move at least 4 spaces, you can Knockback a creature in your path 1 space.
features.manualNote: After moving at least 4 spaces, push a creature in your path 1 space by hand.

name: Oozeling/Construct
description: What even is a “PeOpLe” anyway? So what if your heart pumps oil instead of blood, so what if you don’t even have a heart!? If you can squish yourself into a pair of pants, or swing a sword like everyone else, who’s to say you can’t be a pEOpLe, too?!

features.name: Odd Constitution
features.text: Increment your Hit Dice one step (d6 » d8 » d10 » d12 » d20); they always heal you for the maximum amount. Magical healing always heals you for the minimum amount.
features.manualNote: Hit Dice always heal you for their maximum, and magical healing always heals you for its minimum: apply these by hand.

source.note: Entry starts on printed page 26; the feature text continues on printed page 27.
Entry starts on printed page 26; the feature text continues on printed page 27.

name: Planarbeing
description: You are not from this plane of existence—your soul is not as strongly tethered to it as others. But with this vulnerability comes power, the ability to temporarily shift from one plane to another in times of dire need.

features.name: Planeshift
features.text: –2 max Wounds. Whenever you Defend, you can gain 1 Wound to temporarily phase out of the material plane and ignore all effects of the attack.
features.manualNote: When you Defend and choose to phase out, add 1 Wound and ignore the attack by hand.

name: Ratfolk
description: Ratfolk are survivors, thriving in the shadows of society where others fear to tread. Agile, resourceful, and fiercely loyal to their own, they have a knack for turning scraps into solutions.

features.name: Scurry
features.text: Gain +2 Defense if you moved on your last turn. +1 Speed.

when.situation: You moved on your last turn

name: Stoatling
description: Stoatlings may be small, but they’re far from weak. With fierce determination and warrior hearts, they can capably take down foes many times their size. Their agility and tenacity let them exploit larger enemies’ weaknesses, turning their size into a lethal advantage.

features.name: Small But Ferocious
features.text: Whenever you make a single-target attack against a creature larger than you, roll 1 additional d6 for each size category it is larger. They do the same.
features.manualNote: Add 1d6 per size category the target is larger than you to single-target attacks by hand; larger creatures do the same against you.

name: Turtle/Stonefolk
description: Turtlefolk and Stonefolk take their time in everything they do; they are patient, sturdy, and slow to anger. They rely on their thick shells for protection, making them difficult to harm, but their cautious movements come at the cost of Speed.

features.name: Slow & Steady
features.text: +4 Defense, –2 Speed.

name: Wyrdling
description: Unpredictable and chaotic, Wyrdlings are the result of magic gone awry. Their bodies pulse with raw arcane energy, and their mere presence often disturbs the balance of magic around them.

features.name: Chaotic Surge
features.text: (1/encounter) Whenever you or a willing ally within Reach 6 casts a Tiered spell, you may allow them to roll on the Chaos Table.

action.name: Chaotic Surge
action.text: (1/encounter) Whenever you or a willing ally within Reach 6 casts a Tiered spell, you may allow them to roll on the Chaos Table.

features.manualNote: The caster rolls on the Chaos Table and applies the result by hand.
